Definition: probably from G5143 (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life:--neck.
BiblicalUsage: Peter asks why they would put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples that neither fathers nor they could bear, and the father of the prodigal ran and fell on his neck and kissed him. Peter asks why they would put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples that neither fathers nor they could bear, and the father of the prodigal ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two necks tell the whole story: one bent under a yoke men could not bear, and one embraced by a father who ran to meet his son.
